description: A controlled test of one hypothesis from round 35: Jev under-routes question-shaped turns that sit on hard work, apparently reading `needs_tools: no` as `is easy`. Each pair describes the SAME underlying work twice - once as a question that can be answered in text, once as an instruction that requires editing files. The understanding required is identical; only the output differs. If the question is systematically classified lighter than its paired instruction, the framing is doing the work rather than the difficulty. `difficulty` is the tier the underlying work needs, on the same ladder as the task packs. Expanded in round 39 from 12 pairs to 30, balanced 12 heavy / 10 standard / 8 light, because the original finding moved only three pairs' worth and nothing bounded it beyond the pack. The light pairs are controls: a question about genuinely light work SHOULD be classified light, so a gap that appears there would mean the probe is measuring something other than the effect it claims.

pairs.question: Why does FileBasedCache.has_key raise FileNotFoundError when a cull runs concurrently?
pairs.instruction: Fix the race in FileBasedCache.has_key where a concurrent cull makes it raise FileNotFoundError.
